title: Clothing shop
text: This clothing website has a white background and black Arial letters. A row of links sits under the shop logo. Large coat photos fill the next section. Visitors choose a photo, then a colour and size. The black Buy button turns grey when it is pressed. A bag picture shows the number of items.

title: Supermarket website
text: The supermarket homepage has a red header and a white menu. There are fruit photos below it, with prices under each one. Visitors choose a food section from the menu. They press a plus button beside an item to put it in their basket. The basket price changes at the top of the page.

title: Crafts marketplace
text: Small pictures of bags, bowls and cards cover the homepage. Each picture has the maker's name below it. The headings use Georgia letters, and the prices use Arial. Visitors open a picture to see more photos. A blue button opens the order page. The maker's other work appears at the bottom.

title: Second hand marketplace
text: A yellow logo sits above a long list of items. The background is pale grey, and each item has a white box. A photo is on the left, with the price on the right. Visitors open a box and read about the item. A Message button opens a space for writing to the seller.

title: Technology brand website
text: The first page has a dark background and a large silver phone in the centre. White headings appear above the phone. A small menu runs across the top. Visitors choose a phone colour, and the picture changes. They press See Details to open a page with more pictures, numbers and a Buy button.

title: Restaurant website
text: A photo of the dining room fills the top of the homepage. The restaurant name is written over it in large Georgia letters. The menu has three links: Food, Tables and Contact. Visitors choose Tables, pick a day and time, and write their name. A green button sends the booking, and a message appears below.

title: Bakery website
text: The bakery website uses a cream background and brown headings. Round cake pictures sit below a photo of the shop. Visitors choose a cake picture to read its name and price. The next page has a white order box. After a cake is added, the brown Order button shows a small white tick.

title: Food delivery website
text: An orange header sits above photos of meals. Each meal has its name, price and a red Add button. Visitors first write their address in a box. They then choose food from the list. A white basket stays on the right of the page. Pressing Pay opens a form for the visitor's details.

title: Hotel website
text: The homepage shows a hotel room beside a blue sea. The hotel name sits in a white header above the picture. Visitors choose their dates from two small calendars. A blue Find Rooms button opens a list of rooms and prices. Each room has three photos, a short description and a Select button.

title: Campsite website
text: Green headings sit on a white background. A large photo shows tents beside a lake. The menu is on the left, with links to Prices, Camping and Contact. Visitors choose a camping area on a map. A white box then shows its number and price. A green Continue button opens the booking page.

title: Airline website
text: The airline logo is beside a row of dark blue links. Under the links, visitors choose two airports and a date. A yellow Search button opens the flight list. Times are on the left and prices are on the right. Choosing a price opens another page with a picture of the plane's seats.

title: Transport journey planner
text: The website has two large white boxes on a blue page. Visitors write where they are and where they want to go. A white Search button opens a list of journeys. Each journey shows the bus or train number. A small map appears when a journey is chosen. The map has a green starting point.

title: Tourist guide
text: A mountain photo sits behind the town's name. The words are large and white. Below the picture, three sections show places to eat, sleep and visit. Each section has a photo and a blue link. Visitors open a place and read its address. A map is at the bottom of the page.

title: Museum website
text: The museum homepage has a black header and a pale grey background. A large picture of an old ship sits below the menu. Visitors choose Visit to see opening times and ticket prices. A red Buy Tickets button opens a calendar. After a date is chosen, a white line appears around that day.

title: Art gallery website
text: The gallery name is written in small black letters at the top. Most of the homepage is white. Pictures of paintings sit in one long row. Visitors use arrows to move to the next picture. Pressing a painting opens its own page. The artist's name and the painting's size appear below it.

title: Cinema website
text: Film posters sit in rows on a dark blue page. White Arial letters show the titles and times. Visitors choose a film poster to open its page. A yellow Tickets button shows the times for that day. After choosing a time, visitors see a seat map. Green seats turn white when they are chosen.

title: Theatre website
text: A red header holds the theatre's name and five menu links. A photo of the next show fills the section below. The show title uses large white Georgia letters. Visitors choose a show and then a date. A red button opens the seat map. A white box shows the seats they have chosen.

title: Music festival website
text: The festival website has a purple background and large yellow headings. Photos of singers sit below the dates. Visitors open the Music menu to see each day's shows. A small Play button beside a name starts a song. The Tickets link stays at the top when visitors move down the page.

title: Musician website
text: A black and white photo of the singer fills the homepage. The singer's name is above a small menu. Visitors choose Music to see the album covers. Each cover has a white Play button. The button changes to Pause when music starts. Links to concert dates and the shop are below the albums.

title: Video game website
text: A large game picture sits on a black page. The title has tall orange letters. Three buttons below it say Watch, Play and News. Watch opens a short video in the centre of the page. Play opens a page of game choices. The orange buttons turn white when the pointer moves over them.

title: News website
text: The newspaper name sits above a row of links. The main story has a large photo on the left and a heading on the right. Smaller stories are below it. Visitors choose a heading to read the whole story. A blue Back to Top button appears near the bottom of each page.

title: Online magazine
text: The magazine homepage uses pink headings on a cream background. A large fashion photo is beside the first story. Smaller photos sit in two rows below. Visitors choose a story from a photo or its title. At the end of the story, three more titles appear with small pictures beside them.

title: Travel blog
text: A photo of a bus beside a mountain fills the top of the blog. The writer's name is in white letters over the sky. Below it, visitors see a list of places. Choosing a place opens its stories. Each story has photos between the paragraphs and a box for comments at the end.

title: Recipe website
text: The homepage has a white background, green headings and pictures of food. A menu across the top lists breakfast, lunch and dinner. Visitors choose a meal, then a recipe picture. The recipe page has a photo above the food list. A Print button opens a page with the recipe but no photos.

title: Film review website
text: The website has a black header with a small red star logo. Film pictures sit beside their titles on the homepage. Each title has a number out of five below it. Visitors open a title to read the review. A white box at the bottom lets them write their own comment.

title: School website
text: The school website has a dark green navigation bar beneath a photo of the main building. Links open pages for lessons, news and admissions. The page headings use Georgia, while the smaller text uses Arial. Parents select a year group from a dropdown menu, then open a list of letters with Download buttons.

title: University website
text: A blue university logo sits to the left of a wide search bar. Below it, a video shows students entering a laboratory without sound. Visitors can browse subjects from square picture cards. Selecting a subject opens course details in three tabs. The orange Apply button remains above the tabs while the text changes beneath them.

title: Online learning website
text: The lesson page has a white reading area and a grey sidebar of lesson titles. A blue line appears beside the current lesson. Learners type an answer into an input field and select Submit. A message then appears under the field. They can open a hint or move to the next question with separate buttons.

title: Language learning website
text: The homepage uses a yellow background with round white lesson buttons. Small flags sit beside the language names in the menu. After choosing a language, visitors see lessons arranged by topic. Each lesson opens with a picture and a speaker icon. Tapping the icon plays a word, and a second tap plays it again.

title: Library website
text: A white search bar stretches across the purple header. Visitors can search by book title or author using a dropdown menu beside it. Results appear as small cover images with text on the right. Selecting a title opens a page with availability details. A purple Reserve button opens the member login form.

title: Science website
text: The science homepage has blue headings and a row of planet thumbnails. Visitors choose a planet to open its page. A large diagram appears on the left, while short paragraphs sit on the right. Pressing labelled parts of the diagram opens small information boxes. The boxes close when visitors select the cross in the corner.

title: Children's games website
text: The games homepage uses orange headings and large pictures on a pale blue background. A menu offers word, number and picture games. Children choose a thumbnail, then press a green Start button. During the game, the score appears above the pictures. A round Home icon in the corner returns them to the main menu.

title: Charity website
text: The charity's red logo sits in a white header above a photo gallery. Each photograph has a short caption and a link to a project. Visitors can open a project before selecting Donate. The donation form has three amount buttons and an empty input field. The selected amount has a thick red line around it.

title: Animal rescue website
text: The rescue website shows animal photographs in three columns below a green header. A sidebar contains age and animal type checkboxes. The gallery changes when visitors select a box. Each animal page has several photos, a description and a Contact Us button. That button opens a form with the animal's name already included.

title: Environmental campaign website
text: A photo of a river fills the homepage beneath a narrow black navigation bar. White headings sit over the darker part of the water. Visitors can scroll to a list of local events or use the Join link. Selecting an event opens its date, meeting point and a short registration form on the same page.

title: Volunteering website
text: The homepage begins with a search bar for a town or postcode. Below it, visitors see white job cards on a light blue background. Each card shows a date, place and short task description. Visitors can save a card using a heart icon. Saved jobs appear in a separate tab beside the search results.

title: Council website
text: The council website has a black text logo and a blue menu across the top. Large square links below it show services such as housing and rubbish collection. Selecting a service opens a page with a left sidebar. Visitors can follow the sidebar links or type a question into the search bar above them.

title: Medical clinic website
text: A pale green header holds the clinic name, phone number and opening times. Below it, visitors see three doctor photographs with names and job titles. The Appointments button opens a form with date and time choices. After a time is selected, the form asks for contact details. A message appears when the request is submitted.

title: Gym website
text: The gym website uses black backgrounds, white Arial text and yellow buttons. A weekly timetable appears below a wide photograph of a class. Visitors select a day from seven tabs. Each class has a name, time and Book button. The button changes to a login link if the visitor has not signed in.

title: Sports club website
text: The club colours appear in a striped header behind its logo. A large match photograph is followed by scores and news cards. Visitors can open team pages from a dropdown menu. Each page shows player thumbnails and a fixture list. Selecting a fixture opens ticket choices in a white panel beside the match details.

title: Photography portfolio
text: The homepage opens with a full screen photograph and a small menu in the upper corner. Visitors scroll to a gallery with two columns of images. Selecting a thumbnail opens a larger photograph on a black background. Arrows move through the gallery, while a close icon returns visitors to the same place on the homepage.

title: Design portfolio
text: The designer's name appears in large orange letters above six project thumbnails. A thin black menu links to Work, About and Contact. Visitors choose a project to open a long page of images and captions. The final section contains two arrow buttons, labelled Previous Project and Next Project, above the email address.

title: Author website
text: Book covers sit in a row below the author's photograph. The background is cream, with dark red Georgia headings. Selecting a cover opens a summary and a sample chapter. Visitors can read the chapter on screen or use a Download link. A separate button opens a bookshop website in a new browser tab.

title: Home repair website
text: The repair company's homepage has a blue header with a phone number on the right. Three photographs below it show kitchen, door and window repairs. Visitors select a service to see prices and examples. A Request a Visit button opens a short form. The final field lets visitors add a photograph of the problem.

title: Bank website
text: The bank homepage uses dark blue headings on a white background. A grey navigation bar contains account, card and support menus. Selecting an account opens a page with three tabs for features, costs and documents. The green Open an Account button sits below these tabs. Pressing it begins a form on a separate page.

title: Insurance comparison website
text: A wide form fills the centre of the homepage. Visitors choose an insurance type from four illustrated tabs, then enter their details. Results appear as white cards with prices in blue. A checkbox on each card adds it to a comparison table. The table opens when visitors select the Compare button at the bottom.

title: Property website
text: The website begins with a location field beside price and room menus. After searching, visitors see a map on the right and property cards on the left. Each card has a photo, price and address. Selecting a card opens more photographs. A small heart icon fills with red when the property is saved.

title: Job search website
text: The job website has a white search form on a dark blue header. Visitors enter a job title and town before pressing Search. Results appear below, with checkboxes for hours and pay in a sidebar. Each job opens in a new tab. An Apply button at the bottom opens the employer's application form.

title: Crowdfunding website
text: A large project video sits beside a money total and a green support button. Under the video, tabs open the story, updates and questions. Visitors can choose a support amount from white cards on the right. Selecting a card opens a payment form. The project title and chosen amount remain visible above the form.

title: Discussion forum
text: The forum homepage has blue topic headings and small round member pictures. Visitors open a topic to see its questions in a list. Selecting a question opens the first post and its replies. A Reply button opens a text field beneath the conversation. A preview tab shows the message before the visitor submits it.

title: Supermarket website
text: The supermarket's homepage uses a red and cream colour palette, with bold Arial headings above a grid of offers. Customers begin by entering a postcode, then choose a delivery slot from a weekly calendar. Product cards include photographs and quantity controls. When an item is added, its card briefly gains a red outline and the basket total changes.

title: Second hand marketplace
text: A fixed yellow header contains the marketplace logo, search field and account menu. Search results appear in four columns, with unevenly sized photographs above the prices. Visitors can narrow the list by distance or condition. Opening an item reveals its description and seller details; returning to the results removes the previously selected distance setting.

title: Restaurant website
text: The restaurant website opens with a photograph of an outdoor table beneath a dark green navigation bar. Georgia headings sit above menus written in Verdana. Visitors can switch between lunch and dinner using two tabs. The reservation button opens a white panel over the page, where dates, available times and party size are selected before contact details are entered.

title: Food delivery website
text: The delivery homepage uses orange buttons, pale grey cards and black sans-serif text. Once an address is entered, restaurant cards show photographs, estimated delivery times and fees. Selecting a restaurant opens its food menu beside a fixed basket. Adding an item changes the basket, while selecting Checkout replaces the menu with delivery details and payment fields.

title: Campsite website
text: An illustrated map occupies most of the campsite homepage, with a narrow text menu above it. Different areas are marked by numbered circles rather than photographs. Visitors select a circle to open its description, then follow a link to the booking calendar. On phones, the map extends beyond the screen and can be moved sideways.

title: Transport journey planner
text: The planner uses a dark blue header and large white search fields. A Swap icon exchanges the starting point and destination. After a search, journey cards appear beside a route map, each showing changes and travel time. Expanding a card reveals individual stops. A yellow warning panel appears above the list when part of a route is closed.

title: Museum website
text: The museum's visual identity combines a square red logo with black serif headings and white page backgrounds. A rotating homepage hero displays current exhibitions. Visitors can pause it using a small button below the photographs. The Visit menu opens ticket options, opening times and access information, with each topic arranged as a separate card.

title: Cinema website
text: The cinema website presents film posters in a six-column grid against a charcoal background. Visitors choose a location before viewing screening times. Selecting a time opens a seat plan, followed by a ticket summary and payment page. A row of numbered steps remains above the booking area, and the current step is underlined in yellow.

title: Festival website
text: Large condensed headings sit over a blue and pink background on the festival homepage. Artist portraits form a grid beneath the ticket prices. Visitors can save performers to a personal timetable by selecting a star beside each name. The star fills immediately, while a separate timetable tab lists the selected sets in order of their starting times.

title: Video game website
text: The game website uses a full-width animated landscape behind its homepage title. The navigation is hidden inside a circular icon in the upper corner. Opening it covers the landscape with a black menu. Visitors follow the Download link to choose a device, while a separate News link opens a list of dated development posts.

title: Online magazine
text: The magazine combines oversized serif headlines with narrow columns of sans-serif body text. Its homepage alternates full-width photographs with rows of three article cards. Visitors can browse by subject using a fixed navigation bar. Within an article, selecting a highlighted quotation opens a sharing panel that covers part of the paragraph beneath it.

title: Recipe website
text: The recipe page places a large dish photograph above an introduction and an ingredient list. Green section headings divide the method into numbered stages. A portion control changes the ingredient quantities but leaves the photographs unchanged. Visitors can also enter cooking mode, which displays one stage at a time with Previous and Next buttons below the text.

title: School website
text: The school homepage has a blue header, a white logo and a grid of news photographs. The navigation bar contains six labelled dropdown menus. Parents can open the calendar from any page, then select an event to see its time and location. The mobile layout replaces the navigation bar with a menu button above the school name.

title: Online learning platform
text: The platform divides its course page into a lesson sidebar and a central reading area. Completed lessons have blue ticks, while the current lesson has a darker background. Learners watch an embedded video before opening a short quiz. Submitting an answer displays a written explanation underneath, and the Continue button appears only after the explanation has opened.

title: Library website
text: The library website uses a muted purple header with a white search field beneath its logo. Book results follow a regular grid, although missing covers are replaced by plain grey rectangles. Visitors can change between cover view and a text list. Reserving a book opens the login page, after which the chosen title appears in the member's requests.

title: Children's games website
text: The homepage arranges animal-shaped game buttons around a central tree illustration. Their labels use a rounded sans-serif font, with yellow text on green backgrounds. Selecting an animal opens a game instruction page. A speaker icon reads the instructions aloud, and a square Start button opens the first question without changing the surrounding tree border.

title: Animal rescue website
text: The animal rescue site uses a green and white palette with large portrait photographs. Visitors first choose an animal type, then use age and location filters above the gallery. Each profile includes separate tabs for care needs and visiting arrangements. The enquiry button opens a form containing the animal's name and a field for the visitor's household details.

title: Volunteering website
text: A search panel sits over a photograph of volunteers planting trees. Below it, white opportunity cards show location, duration and task type in matching positions. Visitors can select several cards for a saved list. The Apply button on each card opens an organisation's own website, while the saved list remains in the original browser tab.

title: Medical clinic website
text: The clinic's homepage places a white appointment panel beside a large photograph of its waiting room. Dark green headings use Georgia, while forms use Arial. Visitors choose a service before selecting a clinician and time. Available appointments appear in a vertical list; when none remain, the list is replaced by a link to the next available date.

title: Sports club website
text: The sports club website uses its black and gold colours in the header, buttons and score panels. A wide action photograph sits above the next fixture. Selecting Teams opens a dropdown containing age groups and senior sides. Each team page repeats the same layout, with player photographs above results and a calendar of upcoming matches.

title: Design portfolio
text: The designer presents twelve projects in a grid of square thumbnails on a pale grey homepage. Titles appear below the images in a thin sans-serif font. Visitors can select a project type from a horizontal menu, changing the visible thumbnails. Each project opens a separate page containing sketches, final images and captions beside a numbered project menu.

title: Home repair website
text: The company's blue logo sits above a navigation bar containing service names and a telephone link. The homepage pairs before and after photographs inside sliding frames. Visitors drag the centre line to change the visible area of each photograph. A yellow quotation button opens a form that accepts contact details, a description and up to three uploaded images.

title: Insurance website
text: The comparison page lists insurance plans in horizontal rows with prices on the right. A narrow sans-serif font is used throughout, including in the smaller cost details. Visitors select up to three plans to open a comparison table. The table extends beyond the phone screen, with a scrollbar below the final row.

title: Job search website
text: The job site uses dark blue headings and green Apply buttons on a white background. Search results appear in a left column, while the selected job opens on the right. Visitors can save a vacancy without leaving the results. Selecting Apply replaces the right panel with a form and keeps the job title fixed above it.

title: Discussion forum
text: The forum uses a grey sidebar of subjects beside a white list of recent questions. Each question displays its title, reply count and latest contributor. Opening a thread places the original question above a sequence of replies. Visitors can quote a reply using a small link beneath it, which copies the selected text into the message editor.

title: Clothing shop
text: The clothing homepage places a three-panel campaign beneath a fixed white header, using black sans-serif labels over photographs cropped to identical proportions. Selecting a product opens an image gallery beside size and colour controls. The chosen colour updates both the main photograph and its text label, while an unavailable size remains visible with a diagonal line across its button.

title: Crafts marketplace
text: The marketplace combines cream backgrounds with dark green Georgia headings and a narrow strip of seller portraits. Product results can be displayed as photographs or as a list containing materials and dimensions. When visitors switch views, their filters remain selected; opening a product replaces the results with a gallery, a maker biography and a quotation form beneath the price range.

title: Technology website
text: The product page uses oversized sans-serif headings separated by dark photographic sections, with a horizontal specification menu fixed beneath the main navigation. Selecting a specification scrolls to its section and underlines the corresponding menu label. At the mobile breakpoint, the section menu becomes a dropdown, while the product image changes from a landscape composition to a tighter portrait crop.

title: Bakery website
text: The bakery presents its cakes in a square image grid, using terracotta buttons and cream panels against a white background. Selecting a cake opens a configurator with separate controls for size, filling and collection date. Each choice updates the written order summary, although the main photograph continues to show the original cake throughout the process.

title: Hotel website
text: The hotel page opens with a silent video of the grounds above a booking strip containing dates and guest numbers. Room results appear in paired cards, each with a landscape photograph, an expandable amenities list and a blue selection button. Selecting a room opens a side panel where the nightly price, additional charges and total stay cost appear on separate lines.

title: Airline website
text: The airline's fare table uses a white background, dark blue headings and orange selection outlines. Travellers move from flight results to fare conditions and then to passenger details, with the selected itinerary repeated above each stage. Optional luggage appears in collapsed panels, and opening one reveals illustrated size limits beside a quantity control and an updated total.

title: Tourist guide
text: The destination guide places a searchable map beside a vertically scrolling list of attractions. Selected locations gain a dark outline on the map and expand into cards containing opening times, photographs and transport links. On a narrow screen, the map is replaced by a fixed Map button; closing it returns visitors to their previous position in the list.

title: Art gallery website
text: The gallery uses a near-white background and small black Helvetica labels beneath large artwork photographs. Visitors can change the gallery's background from white to charcoal without leaving the page. Opening an image displays a magnified view, while a separate information button reveals its title, date, dimensions and artist statement in a panel along the right edge.

title: Theatre website
text: A deep burgundy header sits above the theatre's current production photography, with serif titles and sans-serif booking instructions. The performance calendar marks selected dates with an outline and repeats them in a written summary. A visible focus border moves between dates during keyboard navigation, and selecting Continue opens the seating plan while retaining the chosen performance above it.

title: Musician website
text: The musician's homepage has a black background, pale blue typography and an audio player fixed above the footer. Selecting an album changes the track list without replacing the surrounding page. Each track displays its duration and a play control; when playback begins, the control becomes a pause symbol and the current track receives a blue vertical marker.

title: News website
text: The news homepage uses a five-column desktop grid beneath a two-level navigation bar. Headlines appear in a heavy serif typeface, while summaries and timestamps use a lighter sans-serif font. At a narrower width, the sidebar moves below the main stories. The advertising panel retains its desktop width, extending beyond the right edge of the mobile viewport.

title: Travel blog
text: The blog alternates full-width landscape photographs with centred text columns, using Georgia for body text and a condensed sans-serif font for location labels. An interactive route map opens from a fixed corner button. Readers can select a stop to jump to its account, while a small return arrow takes them back to the map without resetting its scale.

title: Film review website
text: The review page pairs a cropped film still with its title, score and publication date. Spoiler sections remain collapsed beneath labelled bars until readers select them. The bars show a plus symbol when closed and a minus symbol when open. Below the article, a rating control displays the visitor's chosen score before a separate button submits it.

title: University website
text: The university course page uses a fixed left menu beside a central column of teaching, assessment and admissions information. Visitors can save a course to a comparison tray, which remains along the bottom edge. Opening the tray displays selected courses in aligned columns; on phones, the same comparison becomes a set of tabs containing one course at a time.

title: Language learning website
text: The lesson interface has a white central panel, dark blue instructions and illustrated answer tiles arranged beneath a sentence. Selecting a tile moves it into the next gap, while selecting a filled gap returns the word to the lower row. Checking an answer adds written feedback below the panel and changes the border around each completed gap.

title: Science website
text: The science article places an animated diagram beside a column of explanatory text, with numbered controls matching labels on the illustration. Visitors can pause the animation or move between stages manually. Below the desktop breakpoint, the diagram appears above the text, and selecting a numbered label opens its explanation in a panel beneath the image.

title: Charity website
text: The charity landing page uses a large documentary photograph above three project summaries, with dark red buttons and black body text. The donation form appears in a white panel over the page. A selected amount receives an outline, while switching between single and monthly giving changes both the form heading and the confirmation text above the payment button.

title: Environmental campaign website
text: Aerial photographs occupy the upper half of the campaign homepage, with small date captions and a green navigation strip below. Visitors can drag a vertical divider across paired images to reveal different years. Beneath the comparison, an expandable panel lists image locations and sources, followed by a registration form with separate controls for events and email updates.

title: Council website
text: The council homepage groups services into labelled panels rather than photographic cards, using dark blue headings and underlined text links. A postcode field opens local collection dates and nearby offices. The result page retains the submitted postcode above its content, and an Edit link reopens the field without clearing the service category already selected.

title: Gym website
text: The gym site uses monochrome training photographs beneath fluorescent yellow navigation labels. A class timetable offers filters for intensity, duration and instructor, with results updating on the same page. Each class expands into a booking panel containing available spaces and a waiting-list option. Selecting the waiting list replaces the booking control with a written confirmation and cancellation link.

title: Photography portfolio
text: The portfolio opens with a monochrome portrait above a three-column grid of photographs cropped to a uniform aspect ratio. Opening a thumbnail displays the uncropped image against a dark background. A small information panel contains the commission, location and date; keyboard arrows move between photographs, while Escape closes the viewer and restores the previous gallery position.

title: Author website
text: The author website uses a cream background, dark green serif headings and line drawings between sections. Visitors can open a sample chapter beside each book cover without leaving the catalogue. A text-size control changes the sample's type size, while the surrounding navigation remains unchanged. Closing the sample returns focus to the button that opened it.

title: Bank website
text: The account page places three product cards beneath a dark blue header, using identical layouts for fees, eligibility and interest details. Selecting Compare opens a table below the cards rather than a new page. Expandable rows reveal additional conditions, and selecting an account opens a separate application whose progress indicator remains above every group of fields.

title: Property website
text: Property results appear beside a map, with price markers matching the cards in the list. Visitors can draw a search area by selecting points on the map, then adjust it by dragging its edges. On mobile, a map toggle replaces the split layout. Opening and closing a property preserves the drawn boundary and the visitor's previous filters.

title: Crowdfunding website
text: The crowdfunding page places a video beside the funding total and reward cards, with a persistent project menu below. Selecting a reward outlines its card and opens a summary containing delivery location, estimated date and total contribution. Additional terms appear through an expandable link, while a Back control returns to the reward list without changing the selected amount.

title: Supermarket website
text: The supermarket interface places a persistent basket beside a product grid whose column count changes at two responsive breakpoints. Quantity controls update the basket without reloading the page, while a written status message appears beneath the altered card. When visitors proceed to delivery, unavailable items are collected in a separate panel containing substitution choices, with the previously selected delivery slot retained above the summary.

title: Crafts marketplace
text: The marketplace's information architecture separates finished goods from commissions, although both routes begin within the same cream and charcoal product grid. Selecting a commission opens a brief form in which material choices reveal additional questions through progressive disclosure. A preview panel reproduces the chosen options beside the maker's photographs, and the final control submits an enquiry rather than collecting payment.

title: Second hand marketplace
text: A map-based results page pairs numbered location markers with seller cards, retaining the same numbering when visitors switch to a list. Photographs are displayed within fixed landscape frames, with uncropped versions available in the item viewer. Opening a seller's profile preserves the search in a background tab, while the message composer inserts the item title above an editable subject field.

title: Technology website
text: The technology brand's homepage combines oversized white typography with alternating video and product-render sections on a black background. A floating comparison control accumulates selected devices in a narrow tray; opening it reveals specifications beneath a row of product silhouettes. At smaller viewport widths, the tray becomes a labelled icon, and each specification category expands independently below the selected device names.

title: Bakery website
text: The bakery's order configurator places a layered cake illustration beside a sequence of labelled choices, using dark brown serif headings over a cream background. Selecting a filling changes a cross-section drawing, whereas selecting a collection date updates a written summary beneath it. Before submission, a final page reproduces every choice alongside an Edit link returning to the relevant stage without clearing subsequent selections.

title: Hotel website
text: The hotel website opens with a panoramic photograph beneath a transparent navigation bar that becomes opaque after scrolling. Booking begins in a compact date panel and continues through room, package and guest-detail screens, each carrying the same itinerary summary. Expanding a price reveals its component charges inline, while changing the dates triggers a fresh availability search without removing the selected guest numbers.

title: Campsite website
text: The campsite page combines an illustrated aerial plan with photographs that open from numbered pitch markers. Visitors may switch between a map and a table displaying dimensions, facilities and availability, with selected pitches outlined in both views. A booking panel remains attached to the lower edge of the viewport, expanding to show dates and guest details when its handle is selected.

title: Journey planner
text: The journey planner presents route alternatives as expandable timelines, with walking sections, interchanges and service alerts distinguished by both symbols and written labels. A control above the results switches between departure and arrival searches without changing the locations. Selecting a disruption opens a panel containing revised timings, while the original itinerary remains visible behind it until a replacement route is confirmed.

title: Tourist guide
text: The destination guide organises its content around neighbourhoods, with each landing page combining an illustrated map, a short introduction and a grid of places. Selected locations accumulate in an itinerary panel that can be reordered by dragging or through adjacent move buttons. The panel displays travel times between stops, and changing the visit date updates opening information without deleting the assembled itinerary.

title: Art gallery website
text: The gallery's near-white pages use small serif captions beneath photographs displayed at their original aspect ratios, producing irregular gaps between rows. Opening an artwork replaces the grid with a full-viewport viewer whose information panel can be expanded independently. The panel contains catalogue metadata, a transcribed artist statement and image credits, while a persistent index records the visitor's position within the exhibition sequence.

title: Cinema website
text: The cinema booking interface places a numbered step indicator above a scalable seat plan, with prices grouped beneath the screen illustration. Seats selected by pointer or keyboard appear in a written summary that remains outside the plan itself. When visitors change screening times, a confirmation panel lists the existing seats before replacing them with the availability for the newly chosen performance.

title: Theatre website
text: The theatre's production pages pair burgundy serif titles with monochrome rehearsal photographs, followed by separate panels for performances, cast biographies and access arrangements. Selecting an access option narrows the calendar to performances carrying the corresponding label. The chosen option persists into the seat-selection screen, where a summary beside the payment control records both the performance date and the selected access details.

title: Musician website
text: The musician's site uses a narrow vertical navigation rail alongside full-height album artwork, with track information set in a monospaced typeface. Playback continues as visitors move between release notes, lyrics and tour dates. The player displays a persistent track title and elapsed time, while opening the merchandise catalogue pauses the background video but leaves the audio controls in their original position.

title: Online magazine
text: The magazine arranges its homepage as an uneven editorial grid, combining large serif headlines with small uppercase category labels and photographs of differing proportions. Article pages replace this composition with a single reading column. Footnote references open short panels beside the relevant paragraph, while the corresponding source list remains available at the end of the article through a labelled navigation link.

title: Travel blog
text: The travel blog presents each journey as a vertical sequence of dated entries interspersed with maps and full-width photographs. A sticky index tracks the entry currently occupying the top of the viewport, while selecting a location marker opens a caption and its associated paragraph. Embedded booking links carry a separate external-link symbol, and their destination names appear alongside the text before selection.

title: Film review website
text: The review page uses a split header containing a film still, publication details and a score panel, followed by body text in a large serif typeface. Spoiler passages are concealed individually rather than as one continuous section. Opening a passage changes its control label to Hide Spoiler, and the expanded text remains in place when the visitor opens a second passage elsewhere.

title: School website
text: The school website divides its primary navigation between current families and prospective applicants, with both routes retaining the same navy header and white emblem. A parent's selection opens a dashboard of notices, forms and calendar entries. Application pages instead present a sequence of stages, with document requirements displayed before the first form and uploaded filenames listed beside individual replacement controls.

title: Science website
text: The science website places an interactive model within a fixed-height frame beside explanatory text, using numbered annotations that remain visible as the model rotates. A transcript tab replaces animation with a written account of each stage. Visitors can adjust playback speed or move through stages individually, while a source panel beneath the model lists publication details and the date of its latest revision.

title: Children's games website
text: The game interface presents a central question panel surrounded by illustrated controls, with an optional text-only view available from the settings menu. Selecting this view removes decorative animation while retaining the question order and answer choices. Feedback appears as both a symbol and a written explanation, and returning to the activity menu preserves the current question beneath a labelled Resume control.

title: Council website
text: The council's service pages use a consistent heading sequence and underlined links, with a location panel positioned above service-specific instructions. Entering a postcode changes collection dates and office information but leaves general guidance intact. Before a form is submitted, a review screen lists the entered details in separate sections, each accompanied by an Edit link that returns to the corresponding fields.

title: Gym website
text: The gym's timetable occupies a white panel beneath a charcoal header, with class categories identified by coloured bars and written labels. Visitors can switch between a weekly grid and a chronological list without resetting their filters. Selecting a recurring class opens a panel offering individual dates or the entire series, and the booking summary identifies each selected session before payment is requested.

title: Sports club website
text: The sports club website places live scores in a narrow strip above its black and amber navigation, while news photographs occupy the main homepage grid. A membership route separates player registration from spectator subscriptions through two labelled cards. Each route opens a different form, with eligibility notes displayed beside the relevant fields and an editable fee summary fixed beneath the final section.

title: Photography portfolio
text: The photographer's portfolio begins with an index of commissions set in small black type, expanding each title into a horizontal sequence of uncropped images when selected. Captions and client credits occupy a separate information drawer. Keyboard controls move between photographs, while a visible position indicator records the current image; closing a commission restores the index at the title from which it was opened.

title: Author website
text: The author's catalogue combines illustrated covers with serif summaries and compact publication metadata, arranged within alternating cream and pale blue sections. A sample-reading control opens an overlay containing adjustable text and a chapter index. Closing the overlay restores focus to its original control, while external purchase links remain grouped by edition and identify the retailer before opening a separate destination.

title: Home repair website
text: The company's quotation journey begins with a service selector beneath a blue navigation bar, then reveals questions specific to the selected repair. Uploaded photographs appear as removable thumbnails beside their filenames, with size limits stated before selection. A review page reproduces the description, contact details and images, and its final button sends the request without displaying a payment field.
